interpretations: Group by town_city only, joining Invoice_Line_Items to Invoices to Orders to Customers. First average product_price and the per-row ratio derived_product_cost/derived_total_cost for each (order_item_id, town). Then average those group averages per town. Compare each town's average ratio to the unweighted mean of the per-town average ratios, and return towns strictly above it.
As interpretation 1, but the cross-town average is the mean of the (order_item_id, town) group-level ratios across all groups, so towns with more groups count for more.
As interpretation 1, but the cross-town average is the mean of the per-row ratios across all invoice line items, regardless of town or grouping.
As interpretation 1, but the ratio at the (order_item_id, town) level is the ratio of averages (avg derived_product_cost / avg derived_total_cost) rather than the average of per-row ratios.

As interpretation 1, but "ignoring missing values" means only rows where product_price, derived_product_cost and derived_total_cost are all non-null are used for both averages. Otherwise each measure ignores its own nulls independently.
As interpretation 1, but rows with derived_total_cost equal to 0 are excluded from the ratio. Otherwise they produce null or an error and are ignored.

As interpretation 1, but the order is reached through Order_Items (via the line item's order_item_id) rather than through Invoices.order_id. These can differ if the invoice's order is not the order of the item.
As interpretation 1, but towns with the same name in different states or countries are treated as separate towns, so the grouping uses town_city together with state_county_province and/or country.

As interpretation 1, but the "how far above" column is the absolute difference (town average ratio minus cross-town average ratio).
As interpretation 1, but the "how far above" column is the relative or percentage difference ((town ratio − overall) / overall).
As interpretation 1, but the output average price is the mean of the group-level average prices (two-level), not the mean of all raw line-item prices in the town.
As interpretation 1, but "above the average" includes ties (greater than or equal) rather than strictly greater.
As interpretation 1, but the results are ordered, for example by the difference descending or by town name. Otherwise they are unordered.

As interpretation 1, but the values are returned at full precision with no rounding. The product_price average may be cast to a numeric type, and the quantities may be treated as numeric rather than text.
As interpretation 1, but the cross-town average is the mean of the other towns' ratios only, leaving out the town being compared.
As interpretation 1, but "how far above" is the multiplicative ratio (town ratio / cross-town average) rather than a difference.

queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT c.town_city AS town_city,
         ili.order_item_id AS order_item_id,
         AVG(ili.product_price) AS avg_price,
         AVG(ili.derived_product_cost * 1.0 / ili.derived_total_cost) AS avg_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Invoices i ON ili.invoice_number = i.invoice_number
  JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.town_city, ili.order_item_id
),
t AS (
  SELECT town_city,
         AVG(avg_price) AS avg_price,
         AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio
  FROM g
  GROUP BY town_city
)
SELECT town_city
FROM t
WHERE avg_ratio > (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM t);
SELECT ili.order_item_id,
       c.town_city,
       AVG(ili.derived_product_cost) * 1.0 / AVG(ili.derived_total_cost) AS cost_ratio
FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
JOIN Invoices i ON ili.invoice_number = i.invoice_number
JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city;
SELECT AVG(product_price), AVG(derived_product_cost)
FROM Invoice_Line_Items
WHERE product_price IS NOT NULL
  AND derived_product_cost IS NOT NULL
  AND derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL;
SELECT order_item_id, invoice_number, derived_vat_payable * 1.0 / derived_total_cost AS ratio
FROM Invoice_Line_Items
WHERE derived_total_cost <> 0;
